answer: I would anchor trust in Signed rental income ledger with tax filings. With rent a landlord declared and taxed for years, a single shale check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so rent a landlord declared and taxed for years stays private; the saffron is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the nadir of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
